bypass_annotation.bypass_reason: The available one-stage quant_from_buffer recipe contracts multiplier and magic-bias addition into one MAC, while W3 requires the binary32 multiplier result to be rounded before nearest-even decode; the frozen-RTL policy excludes a functional RTL fix.
bypass_annotation.contradicted_or_missing_native_path: The fused one-stage path is contradicted by input=400 and multiplier_bits=0x3d828f5c: sequential binary32 MUL then RNE yields 26, but the one-round fused magic model yields 25. No existing typed registry entry materializes a non-contracted shared tail.
bypass_annotation.exact_equivalence_scope: Exactly the frozen 32-element diagnostic occurrence with every lane input int32 400, multiplier binary32 bits 0x3d828f5c, uint8 zero_point 0, finite nonnegative ingress, HWC8 lane order, no tail, and scratch preserving the stage0 binary32 words bit-for-bit. This is not a proof over the shared production domain.
bypass_annotation.materialized_configuration_mechanism: Two serialized native JSON configurations with explicit FP32 scratch: stage0 enables INT32-to-FP32 and uses GA MUL only, writing 32 rounded FP32 words to 0x800000; stage1 reads raw FP32 from 0x800000, uses GA MAC with exact multiplier 1.0 plus magic 12582912.0, applies INT32_SUB raw constant 0x4b400000-zero_point, then enables UINT8 saturation/packing. A separately materialized one-stage fused configuration is the negative control.
bypass_annotation.performance_and_resource_cost: For 32 elements: two configuration launches instead of one; 128-byte scratch allocation; 128-byte scratch write plus 128-byte scratch read (256 extra DRAM bytes); a barrier/lifetime edge between stages; lower utilization and no fusion. Mapping, cycle and contention cost are not measured.
bypass_annotation.unresolved_production_blocker: Full-domain sequential-equivalence, signed INT32 ingress, magic-domain bounds, occurrence/tail generalization, typed handler, mapper, execplan/SCA transport, address allocation, terminal/readback and config-bound RTL simulation remain open. QuantizeLinear additionally lacks an exact binary32 division primitive.
